title: UX audit
metaDescription: UX audit services: heuristic review, analytics and usability findings, and a prioritized list of fixes with effort estimates.

hero.h1: UX audit services that pinpoint where users struggle and why
hero.sub: A heuristic review, analytics deep-dive, and usability findings delivered as a prioritized fix list with effort estimates.

summary: Heuristic review, analytics, and usability findings turned into a prioritized fix list.
sourceContext: US UI/UX design agency; this page sells the UX audit engagement and books audit calls.
abstract: UX audit services review a website or app against usability heuristics, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 criteria and product analytics. Our user experience (UX) audit takes 2–3 weeks, costs $5,000–$15,000, and ends with a prioritized fix roadmap ranked by impact and effort.

sections.answer: A UX audit is an expert evaluation of a website or app that finds usability issues, explains their cause and ranks each fix by impact and effort. Senior designers run the review against usability heuristics, WCAG 2.2 accessibility criteria and product analytics.
sections.body: A UX audit differs from usability testing services in one way: designers evaluate the product, not recruited users. The audit therefore finishes in 2–3 weeks and covers every key user flow, while a usability test covers 3–5 tasks in depth. A website UX audit and an app UX audit follow the same method; only the platform guidelines change.

sections.h2: What does a UX audit include?
sections.answer: Our UX audit services include 6 deliverables: a heuristic evaluation, an analytics review, a session-recording review, an accessibility check, a UX audit report and a prioritized fix roadmap.

items.title: Heuristic evaluation.
items.body: Each key flow is scored with a UX audit checklist built on Jakob Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics, for example visibility of system status and error prevention.

items.title: Analytics review.
items.body: Funnels in Google Analytics 4 show the drop-off points, for example the step where 40 of every 100 sign-ups stop.

items.title: Session-recording review.
items.body: Recordings and heatmaps in Hotjar or Microsoft Clarity show friction points, for example rage clicks and dead clicks.

items.title: Accessibility check.
items.body: Audited screens are checked against WCAG 2.2 level AA, for example colour contrast of 4.5:1 for body text.

items.title: UX audit report.
items.body: Every usability issue gets a screenshot, a severity rating from 1 to 4 and a recommended fix.

items.title: Prioritized fix roadmap.
items.body: Fixes are ranked by impact and effort, with an effort estimate in design and development days.

sections.h2: How does the UX audit process work?
sections.answer: The UX audit process takes 2–3 weeks (10–15 working days) and runs in 4 steps, from kick-off to the roadmap handover.

items.title: Kick-off and goals (1–2 days)
items.body: We agree the user flows, user groups and metrics in scope, and receive analytics access.

items.title: Expert review (5–7 days)
items.body: 2 designers run the heuristic evaluation, analytics review, session-recording review and accessibility check independently.

items.title: Synthesis and scoring (2–4 days)
items.body: Findings are merged, evidenced with screenshots and given a severity rating and an effort estimate.

items.title: Roadmap handover (1–2 days)
items.body: We present the UX audit report in a 60-minute session and hand over the prioritized fix roadmap.

sections.h2: What are the benefits of a UX audit?
sections.answer: A UX audit has 4 benefits: it increases conversion rate, improves the user experience, reduces wasted development time and develops a shared backlog of evidence-based fixes.

items.title: Increases conversion rate
items.body: Removing friction points in checkout, sign-up and onboarding flows increases the share of users who complete them.

items.title: Improves the user experience
items.body: Fixing usability issues and accessibility failures improves task success rate for every user group, including users with disabilities.

items.title: Reduces wasted development time
items.body: Effort estimates show which fixes cost 1 day and which cost 2 weeks, so developers start with the highest impact per day.

items.title: Develops a shared backlog
items.body: Product, design and engineering teams develop one prioritized list, built from evidence instead of opinion.

sections.answer: A UX audit is expert-led and covers the whole product in 2–3 weeks; usability testing is user-led and validates 3–5 tasks with real users. Most teams run the UX audit first, then test the riskiest flows.

sections.h2: How much does a UX audit cost?
sections.answer: A UX audit costs $5,000–$15,000 and takes 2–3 weeks. The price depends on 4 factors: the number of user flows, the number of platforms, the number of user groups and the depth of the accessibility check.
sections.body: A single-platform website UX audit with 3–4 flows sits near $5,000. A web app and mobile app audit with 8–10 flows, 2 user groups and a full WCAG 2.2 AA check sits near $15,000. Teams that need the fixes designed afterwards continue with UX consulting services or a design sprint.

sections.h2: When should a company hire UX audit services?
sections.answer: A company should hire UX audit services in 5 situations:
items: Conversion rate falls, if traffic stays the same.
Support tickets about the same screens rise month after month.
A redesign is planned, if the team has no evidence of what to change.
An accessibility deadline approaches, for example a WCAG 2.2 AA requirement in a contract.
A new product owner inherits a product, if no one documented its usability issues.

sections.answer: These answers cover the 5 questions buyers ask most about UX audit services.

faqs.q: Is a UX audit worth it for a small website?
faqs.a: Yes. A website UX audit of 3–4 flows costs about $5,000 and shows the fixes with the highest impact per development day.

faqs.q: Does a UX audit include accessibility?
faqs.a: Yes. Every UX audit includes a WCAG 2.2 level AA check of the audited screens. A full-site accessibility audit is quoted separately.

faqs.q: Do you need analytics access for a UX audit?
faqs.a: No. A UX audit works without analytics, but Google Analytics 4 or Hotjar access adds drop-off data to the heuristic evaluation.

faqs.q: What is in a UX audit report?
faqs.a: A UX audit report lists every usability issue with a screenshot, a severity rating from 1 to 4, a recommended fix and an effort estimate.

faqs.q: How long does a UX audit take?
faqs.a: A UX audit takes 2–3 weeks, which equals 10–15 working days, from kick-off to the roadmap handover.
